title: Canvas Doctor JSON report envelope
description: The `--format=json` output of `canvas:doctor` (see docs/data-health.md). The envelope — report_version, environment_fingerprint, overall, and each checks entry's type/status/total/healthy/cached/duration_s — is stable: additive changes (new keys, new checks) do not bump report_version, a breaking change does. A check's `details` shape is frozen exactly when this schema constrains it with its own $defs entry; a check validating only against the generic checkEntry makes no such promise, so consume its `details` defensively. This schema tracks HEAD: validate a pinned report against the schema of the same Canvas version.

environment_fingerprint.description: Hash of the Canvas schema version, applied post-updates, and every installed extension's version; decides whether stored per-item results can be reused.

overall.description: Aggregate verdict across every requested check.

healthy.description: True when no check has status "problem". Advisory risks do not affect this.

checks.description: One entry per requested check, keyed by check name. A check with its own $defs entry below freezes its `details` shape. The map is open: a check added by a later release validates against the generic entry.

checkEntry.description: A single check's normalized report entry, shaped uniformly for system and data checks alike so tooling can iterate `checks` without special-casing.

type.description: "system" answers one environment/state question; "data" validates many data items.

status.description: "problem" makes the overall run unhealthy; "risk" is advisory only.

healthy.description: Items with no problem. Risks do not reduce this.

cached.description: Items reused from a prior run instead of revalidated. Always 0 for system checks.

duration_s.description: Wall-clock time for this check, in seconds.

details.description: Per-check payload, unconstrained here; frozen only for checks with their own precise entries.

dataCheckEntry.description: A data check (config, content, the revision checks, auto-save): `details` lists the failing data items and their constraint violations. auto-save findings surface as status `risk`, never `problem`: drafts are allowed to be invalid.

failures.description: One entry per failing finding. Empty when the check is healthy.

finding.description: One validated data item (an entity revision/translation, or an auto-save snapshot) and its violations.

label.description: Human-readable identifier of the data item, e.g. "canvas_page 8 (default revision, nl)".

message.description: The constraint violation message, with any markup stripped.

property_path.description: Path to the offending value, e.g. "components.0.inputs.href". Empty when the violation applies to the whole item.

code.description: The constraint's violation code, when it defines one.

updatesExecutedEntry.description: update_path_executed: the Canvas schema version and its post-update state.

schema_version.description: The schema version the Canvas database is currently at.

applied_post_updates.description: Names of the Canvas post-update functions already applied.

pending_post_updates.description: Names of not-yet-applied post-update functions. Non-empty means results are untrustworthy until `drush updatedb` runs.

codeTaggedReleasesEntry.description: code_tagged_releases: installed extensions that are development checkouts. A dev checkout is an advisory RISK, not a problem: it disables incremental result reuse but never fails the run.

dev_extensions.description: Machine names of installed extensions with no release version. Non-empty disables incremental result reuse and makes this check's status "risk".

updatesEscapedConfigEntry.description: update_path_escaped_config: config entities with a detectable pending migration.

pending.description: Config dependency name => the CanvasConfigUpdater needs*() methods reporting a pending migration for it.
